Midweek, rules for tag checks
New colleagues will find here what to do first

This page covers routine service at the Companion Animal Travel Desk and why it matters. Every tag, note, and handoff protects the traveler, the animal, and the boarding team. We do not work by guesswork. We record service changes in the desk ledger as soon as they are confirmed, then pass the right note to the welcome team and the crew. Keep your tone calm, keep your desk clear, and keep your eyes on the details. A small miss here can delay boarding and unsettle a pet.

Start each interaction by checking the booking against the travel documents and the live service record. Confirm the animal count, carrier status, and any support needed at the gate. If a traveler arrives with a change, update the ledger first, then tell the senior coordinator so the rest of the desk works from the same information. Never rely on memory when a written record exists. If the carrier looks damaged, if the pet seems stressed, or if the paperwork does not match, stop and escalate at once.

Use plain language with travelers. Keep the explanation short and direct, but do not sound rushed. The welcome team depends on accurate notes because boarding moves fast and the crew needs practical instructions before the handoff. If a traveler asks for help, stay with the facts and avoid promises you cannot confirm. When the desk is busy, move one file at a time and finish the entry before taking the next task. This keeps errors from spreading across the shift.

Pay special attention to tag checks, service changes, and any movement between counters. If Mochi or any other pet is marked for extra care, make sure that note is visible to the team that will meet the traveler next. Remember that each journey is a shared responsibility, and careful desk work is what keeps it safe. Remember: write it down, pass it on, and check it again.
